solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stable lad can be trained

indicators.note: something trained is drilled into a new shape, so these letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A stable lad who can be trained to look after the horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable lad' reads as one stable worker, but 'Stable' is the definition and 'lad can be' is the fodder that 'trained' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is steady and evenly poised, which is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Distinctive odours, as evident around Italian's capital

indicators.note: the small word goes around the city, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
Roma is the Italian name for Rome, Italy's capital

explanation.surface: Distinctive smells are evident all around the Italian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromas are distinctive smells, typically pleasant ones such as cooking scents.

clue.text: A female with wrath that is burning

parts.note: ire is anger, wrath

explanation.surface: A woman whose anger is blazing.
explanation.definitionFit: Afire is a literary word for on fire, so burning.

clue.text: Grabbed by bounder, simpleton is kissed and cuddled

indicators.note: being grabbed by something means being held within it, so one word is inside the other

parts.note: a cad or bounder is a dishonourable man
noodle is old slang for a fool or simpleton

explanation.surface: A simple soul is seized by a rogue and smothered with kisses.
explanation.walkthrough: A noodle is old slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle amorously, so canoodled is the past tense.

clue.text: Senior journalist upset his colleagues generally, bringing dismay

definitions.note: a phrase meaning to bring dismay, matching the verb

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the senior journalist
the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: An editor annoyed fellow journalists in general and made them miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suits a down clue, where the editor's abbreviation is turned upside down; 'the press' is journalists as a body.
explanation.definitionFit: To depress someone is to sadden them, to cause gloom and dismay.

clue.text: Tree found in part of London

definitions.meaning: a tall fast-growing tree of the willow family
a district of east London in the Docklands, in the borough of Tower Hamlets

explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a common tree, and Poplar is also an East London district named after such trees.

clue.text: Effectiveness of cosmetic daughter denied

indicators.note: something denied is refused or kept out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: face powder is a cosmetic

explanation.surface: A daughter is refused a make-up product for its effectiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: Power is the capacity to have an effect, which is effectiveness.

clue.text: That posse goes out as quickly as possible

indicators.note: going out suggests breaking ranks and scattering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The sheriff's posse rides out at full speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-haste means with great speed, as quickly as a post rider could go.

clue.text: A stucco I fancy as characteristic of auditorium?

indicators.note: fancy here is a verb or adjective of elaborate whim, so the letters are arranged decoratively anew

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a stucco ceiling as typical of a concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall's acoustic is how sound behaves inside it, the quality that marks out a good auditorium.

clue.text: Gesture with heavenly body — it's received the wrong way!

indicators.note: the heavenly body takes in, or receives, the other piece within itself

parts.note: the moon is a heavenly body

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the little word is read from right to left

parts.note: the 's here is 'is', a link, leaving the word it

explanation.surface: Someone gestures towards a heavenly body that has been seen in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' reverses the little word, and 'received' puts it inside the heavenly body; the 's of 'it's' is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion is a movement of the hand or body made to convey a meaning, a gesture.

clue.text: Dad gets shown reconstructed piano in uncle's place

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: something reconstructed is rebuilt in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Dad has a rebuilt piano displayed at his uncle's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, so his place is the shop where goods are pledged. 'reconstructed' rearranges SHOWN plus P into WNSHOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, so uncle's place is the pawnbroker's shop.

clue.text: Observe what shopkeeper may do before giving change

definitions.meaning: to observe is to pay attention to something

definitions.text: what shopkeeper may do before giving change
definitions.meaning: a shopkeeper accepts a banknote from the customer before handing back change

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means pay attention, and literally describes accepting a banknote from a customer at a till.

clue.text: The woman's brought back wood — old stuff being used again

indicators.note: bringing back means the word is turned to run the other way

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
ash is a hardwood tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A woman fetches back old timber to be reused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses the pronoun only; 'wood' follows unchanged. The definition is the long phrase at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehash is old material presented again with little real change, a recycling of stale stuff.

clue.text: Spanish males engaged in art of commerce

indicators.note: engaged here means busy at work, set in motion, so the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Spanish men are busy in the business of trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' looks like part of the picture of men at work; 'engaged' is the anagram signal for SPANISHMALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Salesmanship is the skill of selling, which is the art at the heart of commerce.

clue.text: Piece of wood to lean in hanging support

indicators.note: the leaning word goes inside the support

parts.note: a sling is a band hanging from the neck to support an arm
to cant is to tilt or lean

explanation.surface: A piece of timber is left leaning in a hanging sling.
explanation.definitionFit: A scantling is a small beam or timber of set dimensions, a piece of wood.

clue.text: One science unit in a valley still to let?

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the valley phrase

parts.note: a vale is a valley
I is the Roman numeral for one
a lab is a laboratory, a unit where science is done

explanation.surface: A science laboratory built in a valley is still waiting for a tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: The query marks the definition as an example: a property still to let is available.
explanation.definitionFit: A property still to let is free to be taken up, which is the sense of being obtainable.

clue.text: Soldier gives sign for pausing followed by frantic nod

parts.note: a comma is a punctuation mark showing a short pause

indicators.note: frantic means wildly agitated, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A soldier signals a halt and then nods frantically.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier trained for raids, so it is a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Two things (semi-competent?) violinist might do to be obsequious?

definitions.meaning: a violinist bows the strings, and a poor one makes a scraping noise
to behave in a servile, fawning way

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to fawn or grovel, originally from the deep bow with the foot drawn back.

clue.text: Order chaps in court to provide explanatory note

indicators.note: the order and chaps go inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A judge orders the men in court to submit an explanatory note.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To comment is to remark on something, giving an explanatory note on it.

clue.text: Stupid person crossing road was a famous general

indicators.note: crossing here means stretching across, so one word spans the other inside it

parts.note: a goon is a stupid person

explanation.surface: A fool crossing the road turned out to be a famous general.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Gordon, 'Gordon of Khartoum', was a famous British general of the Victorian era.
explanation.definitionFit: General Charles Gordon, killed at Khartoum in 1885, is a famous British general.

clue.text: Hits coming from small child in the middle of lesson

indicators.note: the child's word sits inside the letters taken from lesson
the middle of a six-letter word is its central pair of letters

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Blows are struck by a little child during a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small child' is one phrase, not S plus a child; 'the middle of lesson' supplies the two central letters, which 'in' places around the child.
explanation.definitionFit: To smite is to strike hard, so smites is an old-fashioned word for hits.

clue.text: Land by sea gets temporary support

definitions.meaning: the land along the edge of the sea
a prop or beam set up to hold a wall temporarily

explanation.definitionFit: The coast is land beside the sea; a shore is also a timber prop shoring up a structure.

clue.text: Instrument with which this person has left theatre

parts.note: this person is the setter speaking of himself, me
Odeon is a classical name for a theatre or concert hall, and a chain of cinemas

explanation.surface: The person who walked out of the theatre took an instrument along.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodeon is a small accordion or reed organ, a musical instrument.

clue.text: Director, foul, had G&T maybe

parts.note: rank means foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A director, a foul person, had a gin and tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: G&T is gin and tonic; 'maybe' marks it as an example of what was drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a gin and tonic is one example of consuming a drink, so the past tense of drink fits.

clue.text: I'd not eat nasty poison? Certainly not!

definitions.text: I'd not eat nasty poison? Certainly not!

indicators.note: nasty suggests something gone bad or twisted, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner refuses to swallow some nasty poison.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: 'nasty' rearranges IDNOTEAT, and the remedy is the very opposite of a poison.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote counteracts a poison, which is the opposite of what the clue's poison would do.

clue.text: Drink — the next thing on from Product X?

parts.note: a brand is a manufacturer's product line
the letter after X in the alphabet is Y, so the next thing on from Brand X is Brand Y

explanation.surface: A drink is the next thing to follow on after Product X.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand X' is the advertisers' name for an unnamed rival product; 'the next thing on from' it is Brand Y, as Y follows X.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, a drink.

clue.text: Dancing round in truck

indicators.note: the round shape is placed inside the truck word

parts.note: a bogie is a wheeled undercarriage or small railway truck
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: People dance around inside a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: A bogie is a wheeled truck, as on a railway, not the lorry the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Boogie is lively dancing to pop music; as a verb, to boogie is to be dancing.

clue.text: We in the army will want ruler to be changing slightly

indicators.note: the pronoun goes inside the army abbreviation

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
taken as written
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Soldiers in the army will want their ruler to change a little.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweaking means making small adjustments, so changing something slightly.
